events.title: Mango in season
events.category_name: Food, cooking, and eating it with people
events.applies_to_note: Available to essentially anyone, anywhere
events.requires_note: Needs nothing but being alive and present
events.summary: It is available for a few weeks and then it is not. The season is short and everyone knows when it starts. Costs almost nothing, needs no permission from anybody, and is one of the few good things in this dataset that nothing can attach to.

details.aspect: The first one of the year
details.description: You have not had a mango since last year and the first one resets something. The rest of the season is spent chasing that first one.
details.energy_note: A taste you had forgotten you were waiting for.

details.description: People who grew up with mangos know the week it begins without checking. The anticipation starts before the fruit does, which is the part the research says is free.
details.energy_note: Looking forward to it is most of it.
details.notes: Kumar, Killingsworth & Gilovich: anticipation of experiences is pleasurable and unrelated to cost.

details.description: Almost nobody eats the first mango of the season alone. It is given, split, or brought back for you by someone who was passing the market.
details.energy_note: Given, rather than bought.

details.description: No document, no permit, no border, no electricity, no institution. A few coins at most, and often not even that.
details.energy_note: Nothing on earth has to approve this.

details.aspect: It becomes a marker for the year
details.description: Decades later the smell of a mango puts you in one specific childhood kitchen. It is doing memory work you never asked it to do.
details.energy_note: A fruit that files your whole childhood.

events.title: Jollof rice
events.category_name: Food, cooking, and eating it with people
events.applies_to_note: Available to most people, given ordinary circumstances
events.requires_note: Needs at least one other person
events.summary: The pot everyone has an opinion about. A cooked thing, made or bought, and mostly the point is who is at the table rather than what is on it.

details.description: The pot everyone has an opinion about. Eaten hot, or eaten cold later, and both are correct.
details.energy_note: It is good. That is the whole of layer one.

details.description: The shopping, the chopping, the waiting, the smell filling the place forty minutes before anyone eats. For a lot of people this is the better half.
details.energy_note: The kitchen smelling of it, before anyone sits down.

details.description: Almost no one lists a meal among their best days because of the food. They list it because of the table. The Harvard Study has been saying a version of this for eighty-seven years.
details.energy_note: The table, not the plate.
details.notes: Harvard Study of Adult Development: relationship quality is the strongest predictor of health and happiness.

details.description: Money for ingredients, a working cooker, somewhere to sit, and people free at the same time. Any of those can fail.
details.energy_note: Four ordinary things, and any of them can be missing.

details.description: Eventually you make it the way one specific person made it, including the part they did wrong, because that is how it is supposed to taste.
details.energy_note: Cooking someone else's mistake, deliberately.

events.title: A holiday in the next town over
events.category_name: Travel, elsewhere, and coming back
events.applies_to_note: Available to most people, given ordinary circumstances
events.requires_note: Needs to move around your own town
events.summary: Forty minutes and a different market. Nothing to do and nowhere to be. Administratively free.

details.description: Forty minutes and a different market. The first morning you wake up somewhere that is not where you live is worth most of what it cost to get there.
details.energy_note: Waking up somewhere else.

details.description: The weeks before going to the next town over are their own good thing. Kumar, Killingsworth and Gilovich found anticipation of an experience is pleasurable in itself and, notably, unrelated to what it cost.
details.energy_note: The waiting is part of the thing, not a delay before it.
details.notes: Waiting for Merlot: anticipatory consumption of experiential and material purchases.

details.description: Asked years later what made the trip to the next town over good, people name the company rather than the content. The Harvard Study of Adult Development has been producing that result for eighty-seven years.
details.energy_note: The people, not the thing.
details.notes: Harvard Study of Adult Development: relationship quality is the strongest single predictor of health and happiness.

details.aspect: What it takes to be allowed
details.description: Nothing but the fare and the time off.
details.energy_note: The only obstacle is the fare.

details.description: The trip to the next town over stops being an event and becomes a reference point - retold, compared against, and eventually shorthand inside one family for a whole kind of day.
details.energy_note: It turns into the story about it.
details.notes: Experiential purchases retain value through memory where material ones decay; people are markedly unwilling to trade the memory away.

events.title: The first mouthful of tea in the morning
events.category_name: Small sensory goods: the tiny reliable pleasures
events.applies_to_note: Available to essentially anyone, anywhere
events.requires_note: Needs nothing but being alive and present
events.summary: A small, cheap, repeatable good. The savoring literature is direct about these: it is less the objective density of nice things that makes a day good than whether they are noticed and amplified.

details.description: The first mouthful of tea in the morning. Four seconds to a couple of minutes. Costs nothing or almost nothing, and is available most days to most people.
details.energy_note: Small, and reliably there.

details.description: Humans have finite attention and negative stimuli dominate it, so people are not naturally prone to savouring. It is a practised capacity, and practising it prospectively predicts more uplifts later.
details.energy_note: It only counts if you catch it.
details.notes: Amplifying savoring predicted increased uplift frequency over three months; the causal arrow runs from attention to experience.

details.description: Unusually for this dataset, this family does not need anybody else, which is why it survives isolation, displacement and night shifts when almost nothing else in these files does.
details.energy_note: Available even when everything else has been removed.

details.description: Almost nothing, which is the point of including fifty of them. In a game where every other good thing attaches to a hurdle, these are the rows that cannot be taken away by a visa officer.
details.energy_note: Nothing on earth has to approve this.

details.aspect: It compensates for a thin day
details.description: People low in both uplifts and savoring showed low positive affect and life satisfaction; the other three groups were similar. A strong capacity to savour genuinely offsets a day with few good things in it.
details.energy_note: Enough of these makes a bad week survivable.
